text:
Mia: Heads up — customer (tiered bank) wants BYOK for Private deployment with cross-region DR (us-east/us-west). Requirements they called out: no Redwood personnel can access raw customer keys; operator-assisted import for disaster recovery with JIT approvals; full, tamper-evident audit trail for every import/use for SOC2/PCI review. How do we map custody boundaries and what RBAC changes do we need? cc @Jordan @Samir @Lisa

Jordan: For RBAC I'd propose a dedicated 'custody-importer' role scoped only to the import API + an MFA-protected JIT approval flow. Ephemeral creds for the import window, and a separate 'audit-reader' role that can see metadata/events but never key material. Also: require a signed proof-of-possession (PoP) from the customer as part of import. :thinking: 

Samir: Infra notes — import pipeline should accept only wrapped blobs and PoP. We must do agent attestation + HSM firmware checks before allowing import. Any import must emit a canonical event with trace-id, operator id, cert serial and HSM fw version. Store only wrapped blobs; never persist unwrapped key.

Mia: +1 on PoP and agent attestation. Customer insists on contractual guarantee that we cannot unwrap keys. Can we clearly document how custody boundary prevents unwrap (e.g., we never hold unwrapping key material, and import happens inside customer-owned HSM or with customer-signed PoP)? Need language we can hand to legal.

Lisa: Legal: we'll need explicit contract clauses about no-Redwood-unwrap, incident notification SLAs, and log retention/residency minimums. Also check whether customer requires independent attestation of our import flow (third-party audit). For retention, propose default 7 years for import events with opt-down allowances.

audit-bot: audit-bot: Automated check: current audit schema missing 'key_import_actor_type' and 'hsm_fw_version' fields which compliance wants. Created ticket SEC-1128 to add fields and backfill for last 90 days.

ops-oncall: For IR: if an import fails or suspicious import pattern is detected, runbook should include immediate suspension of the 'custody-importer' role, snapshot of HSM audit logs, export of canonical events (trace-id), and a forensics handoff to security/legal. We should define SLA for customer notification (e.g., 1hr for suspected compromise).

Samir: Vulnerability catch — CVE-2024-XYZ affects certain HSM firmware versions. We should block imports from HSMs with fw < 5.2.2 and surface a human-readable reason to operator. Also create a migration/patching plan and customer notification template.

Jordan: Implementation sketch: 1) Add 'custody-importer' RBAC role + JIT UI (approval ticket with MFA). 2) KMS API endpoint ImportKey(wrapped_blob, PoP, metadata) -> returns key_id + import_audit_event. 3) Audit event schema includes trace-id, actor(id+type), cert_serial, hsm_fw, import_result. 4) Enforce HSM fw whitelist and attestation in pipeline. Estimated work: 2 sprints (backend + UI + audit schema).

Mia: Action items: Jordan — prototype RBAC + ticket UI and open RFC. Samir — draft HSM import pipeline, fw-check gating, and sample logs. Lisa — draft contract language & retention options. ops-oncall — update runbook and schedule a tabletop drill for key-import compromise scenario. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow. :calendar:

Jordan: Noted. I'll open SEC PR that includes schema diffs and a mock of the JIT approval flow (screenshots + API).

Samir: Sample import event we should emit (for reference):
```
IMPORT EVENT trace=trc-abc123 actor=operator-jon actor_type=custody-importer cert=serial:da34 wrapped_len=4096 result=success hsm_fw=5.2.1 attestation=passed
```
Mia: Thanks all — please ping if you hit blockers. Leaving thread for now. :thumbsup:
